name: How to be a tester — Daraja Friends Test
playIn: Shown as text on the friends page (📖 Read: how to be a good tester). No recorded video yet: watch.html?mode=explain reads kenya/ only.
lines: Thank you for helping. This short note explains what we are asking you to do, and why it matters so much.

First, what is Daraja? Daraja means bridge in Swahili. Daraja Studio is Jerry's small family business. It makes simple apps for families, churches and small businesses. They open in the web browser on your phone, so there is nothing to install.
The profits from the apps help students in Kenya stay in school. So every app you help improve helps a student, too.

Why do we need you? Because the people who build an app cannot see its problems. They know where every button is. You do not. You are seeing it for the first time, and that is exactly what makes your eyes so valuable.
Please remember: you are not being tested. The app is. If something confuses you, that is the app's fault, and it is exactly what Jerry needs to hear.
Each test has four parts, always in the same order.
Part one: a short video. It explains what the app is for, who uses it, and the main screens. Watch it once, with the sound on. If you cannot listen right now, tap Read it instead.

Part two: the steps. They tell you exactly what to do, one step at a time, and what you should see. After each step, tap It worked, It didn't, or Not sure. If something did not work, write what happened in your own words. A few words is plenty.

Part three: the challenge. The app starts empty. You get a few small jobs to do, but nobody tells you which buttons to press. You use what you learned. When you finish, tap Check my work. The checker looks at what the app really saved, and marks each job. If a job is not right yet, you get a hint and one more try.
Part four: one question. In your own words, what is this app for? There is no wrong answer. We want to know what you understood.
Before every challenge, a card says Pretend you are, and tells you who you are and what you need today. Try to think like that person.

Each app opens in its own tab. Do the step there, then come back to the test page tab. If you get lost, pull the app page down to reload it. Your answers on the test page are saved after every tap, so you can stop and come back any time.
If you get stuck, tap I'm stuck. It gives you a hint, and if that does not help, you can skip the step with a short note. A skipped step with a note is useful information, too.
Honest beats fast. A red cross that finds a real problem is worth much more than a quick green tick. Confusing words, small print and hidden buttons are all real problems.

A few practical things. On an iPhone, use Safari. On Android, use Chrome. If the words are too small, tap the A a plus button at the top of the test page. And please type only the made-up names and numbers the test gives you, never your real passwords, bank details or private family information.
There is no payment for testing, and it never costs you anything. As a thank-you, Founding Testers get their first year of the Family and Later-life membership free, then half price for life.

Everyone starts with the same app, One Thing. It shows just one thing to do at a time, for anyone whose mind runs fast or whose to-do list feels like a wall. Please take your time with it: it is the app we care about most.
Take your time. Be curious. Be honest. And thank you, from Jerry and the whole family, for helping us build a better bridge.
